- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (last 5–7 days of forecast) — adjust downward bias by +2–3% for the final 10 days.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model overcorrects — apply a slight upward bias to counteract.  
- Forecast often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after day 3–5, adjust forecast to rise 1–2 days ahead of the sentiment peak.  
- Avoid overreacting to early sentiment spikes — if sentiment rises sharply on day 1–2, model should not immediately peak — delay peak by 1–2 days.
